purpose: Present a controlled one-based page position, result range and optional page-size selector for a host-owned result set.
anatomy: numbered page buttons and visual gaps
behaviorProvider: Native nav, buttons and select; Aegis calculates a bounded display window from host props.

component: label boundary controls and current page
host: actual paging, fetching and accepted page state

requirements.statement: For display, normalize a finite total to a nonnegative integer, a finite pageSize to at least one and a finite page to the one-based valid range. Nonfinite values fall back to total=0, size=25 and page=1 respectively.
Update page in response to onPageChange and apply it to the underlying dataset or request. Display normalization does not call back to correct invalid host state or fetch records.
The polite summary reports 0 plus noun for an empty total, otherwise the current inclusive item range and total. The page count remains at least one even for zero results.

Disable Previous at the first page and Next at the last page; zero results or disabled disables all page navigation buttons. Each numbered button identifies its page and the current one exposes aria-current=page.

Always include valid first/last pages and the current neighborhood, adding near-edge neighbors as needed, deduplicating and sorting. Gaps render as aria-hidden ellipses rather than navigable controls.

Render the size select only when onPageSizeChange exists. A size change calls onPageSizeChange with the numeric selected value, then calls onPageChange(1); the host must accept both updates coherently.

Supply finite positive integer pageSizeOptions suitable for the dataset. The component deduplicates finite positive choices and includes the normalized current size, but does not integer-normalize the supplied option values.
Pagination buttons use type=button and must not submit an enclosing form. The size control has an associated Rows per page label and uses native select keyboard behavior.
Set disabled while page changes must be blocked and own any focus/announcement policy for newly loaded content. Pagination does not move focus to the result region or provide loading/error UI.
Use navigation group tokens for controls and input-modality focus styling. Keep the display range and disabled semantics independent of theme and density decisions.

limitations: Pagination does not store pages or perform a fetch; the host remains authoritative.
The noun and Rows per page label are not a comprehensive localization API.
Accepted host inputs should be finite positive integer sizes even though the display applies defensive normalization.
